description: Issue #824 Part 1 / B1.1: neutralizes UpdateModelProperty's new FileAttachment-FK guard condition (compile-preserving operator: `dc.IsFileAttachmentForeignKeyProperty(entityType, prop.Name) && false`, never a deletion) so it can never fire, and checks it against MvcAuthHolesTests' HTTP-layer regression test. The posted value in that test is a REAL, persisted FileAttachment id (seeded under a DIFFERENT tenant) rather than a garbage GUID. PR #978 (#824 Part 2) review: the ORIGINAL red_test here (UpdateModelProperty_FileAttachmentForeignKey_RejectedButNonAttachmentFieldSucceeds) can no longer detect this mutation on its own -- Part 2's independent FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard boundary now also rejects the same forged write with an equivalent-looking message, so neutralizing Part 1 alone no longer changes that test's outcome (defence in depth from the caller's side, but useless as a Part-1-specific mutation signal). red_test now points at UpdateModelProperty_FileAttachmentForeignKey_Part1GateAlone_RejectedWithBoundaryGuardDisabled, which disables Part 2 via FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard.Enabled = false for its duration so this mutation has nothing left to catch the forged write -- the request succeeds (200) instead of failing (400) -- isolating Part 1's own contribution again. green_tests is a sibling MVC-004 test (Password blocklist) proving this mutation's blast radius is scoped to the new guard and does not collaterally affect the independent blockedFields check.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.MvcAuthHolesTes: #824 Part 1 alone \(boundary guard disabled\): a FileAttachment FK \(PhotoId\) must still be rejected by Part 1's own field-level gate\. Got 200

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first, Release build, #959) with the mutant patch applied: 'Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<BadRequest>. Actual:<OK>. #824 Part 1 alone (boundary guard disabled): a FileAttachment FK (PhotoId) must still be rejected by Part 1's own field-level gate. Got 200: {"Msg":"success","Code":"200","Data":"Success"}'. Confirmed identical on a second independent run_mutant.py invocation (determinism check).
